columns.label: Symbols (1)
columns.means: Letters that change how the row is read. “A” means the entry only applies to air shipments, “D” that the name suits domestic shipments, “G” that you must add a technical name, “I” that it comes from the international list, “W” that it applies to water only, and “+” that the name, class and packing group are fixed as printed.

columns.label: Proper shipping name and description (2)
columns.means: The name the shipment must be described by. An entry reading “see …” is a pointer to the entry you should actually use.

columns.label: Hazard class or division (3)
columns.means: The kind of danger: 3 is a flammable liquid, 8 corrosive, 9 miscellaneous, and so on. “Forbidden” means the material may not be offered at all.

columns.label: Identification number (4)
columns.means: The UN, NA or ID number that goes on the package and on the shipping paper.

columns.label: Packing group (5)
columns.means: How dangerous the material is within its class: I is the worst, III the least. It drives which packagings you may use.

columns.label: Label codes (6)
columns.means: Which hazard labels the package must carry, by code. The first code is the primary hazard; any others are subsidiary.

columns.label: Special provisions (7)
columns.means: Codes that add to, or except you from, the normal rules. Their words are printed at 49 CFR 172.102.

columns.label: Exceptions — packaging (8A)
columns.means: The section of 49 CFR Part 173 that may let you out of the full rules, for example as a limited quantity. “None” means there is no exception.

columns.label: Non-bulk packaging (8B)
columns.means: The Part 173 section that says which non-bulk packagings are authorised.

columns.label: Bulk packaging (8C)
columns.means: The Part 173 section that says which bulk packagings are authorised.

columns.label: Passenger aircraft or rail limit (9A)
columns.means: The most you may put in one package on a passenger aircraft or a passenger railcar. “Forbidden” means it may not go that way at all.

columns.label: Cargo aircraft only limit (9B)
columns.means: The most you may put in one package on a cargo-only aircraft.

columns.label: Vessel stowage location (10A)
columns.means: Where the package may be stowed on a ship: A on deck or under deck, B, C, D and E are progressively more restricted.

columns.label: Vessel stowage other (10B)
columns.means: Extra stowage conditions on a ship, by code, printed at 49 CFR 176.84.
